tools.name: render_invoice
tools.description:
Render an XML e-invoice (UBL or CII, e.g. XRechnung) as a readable HTML page.

invowerk uses the KoSIT XRechnung visualization. Use it to show a person what
an e-invoice contains.

Input: `invoice_base64` is the base64 of the XML, at most 4 MB decoded, or pass
the file as a download link in `file`.

tools.name: explain_errors
tools.description:
Explain rule codes in plain language. Works without an API key.

Covers the codes of `validate_invoice` findings and hints: EN 16931,
XRechnung, ZUGFeRD and invowerk's own hint codes (IW-*).

Input: `codes` is a list of one or more codes, e.g. ["BR-CO-18", "BR-DE-21"].
Duplicates are removed. `lang`

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "generate_invoice" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: validate_invoice, generate_invoice, convert_invoice · Private data: validate_invoice, render_invoice, explain_errors, generate_invoice, parse_invoice, convert_invoice · Public sink: generate_invoice · Destructive: parse_invoice.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: validate_invoice, generate_invoice, convert_invoice · Private data: validate_invoice, render_invoice, explain_errors, generate_invoice, parse_invoice, convert_invoice · Public sink: generate_invoice · Destructive: parse_invoice

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
